Each repo runs its own build under vx and under the tool it ships with,
on the same machine and the same tasks; medians of interleaved reps. vx
first, theirs second; **bold** marks the other tool winning.

Every row below ran vx without a lock, evaluating every config per run.
The harness (`packages/vx-bench/real/`) now takes a `vx lock` once per
repo and runs vx `--frozen`, as CI does; a row re-measured that way
will say so.

## Where the other tool wins

- **payloadcms/payload** (Turbo). A tie within noise. On every hit vx stats all 14,430 recorded output files to prove they are intact; Turbo checks nothing on disk. [Details](../#payloadcmspayload-45-build-tasks-pnpm-10-turbo-2104).
- **n8n-io/n8n** (Turbo). The cold build is `n8n-nodes-base#build`, 55 s alone, plus what fits around it; vx is 2.6% behind there. [Details](../#n8n-ion8n-70-build-tasks-pnpm-12-turbo-2918-node-24).
- **unocss/unocss** (Turbo). One task, `@unocss/vscode#build`, rewrites its own `README.md` input on every run. vx will not save a result whose input changed under it, so it reruns that task each time; the other 41 are a 160 ms no-op. [Details](../#unocssunocss-turbo-21013-turbo-f05ee3a).
- **vueuse/vueuse** (Turbo). Turbo restores this repo faster, and its no-op alternates: its key for one task flips between two values on consecutive runs, so every other no-op rebuilds (7.3–7.7 s). [Details](../#vueusevueuse-turbo-21012-turbo-efdd69a).
